title: Two Piles With the Same Sum

concept.title: Find one subset with half of the total
body: Splitting the numbers into two piles with equal sums means: the total is even, and some subset has the sum `total / 2` (the other numbers then also add up to `total / 2`). So the question is whether **one subset reaches a given target**.
The search takes or leaves each number and stops at the **first** success: if the target is reached, return `True` at once and let all the calls above return `True` too.

The `or` is lazy: if the first call returns `True`, the second one is not even started. A search that looks for **one** solution can stop early; a search that has to count or list all solutions cannot. If the total is odd, the answer is `no` without any search.

statement: Given `n` positive integers, decide whether they can be split into two piles with the same sum. Every number goes to exactly one of the piles.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.

examples.note: The total is 8. The piles {3, 1} and {1, 2, 1} both have sum 4.

hints: If the total is odd, the answer is no.
Otherwise look for any subset whose sum is half of the total.
For every number take it or leave it, and stop as soon as the missing amount is 0 or negative.

solution.complexity: Time O(2^n) in the worst case, space O(n).
